subsystems.name: Sample and sequencing
subsystems.role: obtains DNA from the patient and reads its sequence.

subsystems.name: Bioinformatics pipeline
subsystems.role: turns raw sequence reads into a list of genetic variants.

subsystems.name: Interpretation and evidence
subsystems.role: decides which variants are clinically actionable and what treatment they suggest.

subsystems.name: Diagnostic test
subsystems.role: confirms the key biomarker in a regulated, reproducible assay.

subsystems.name: Therapeutic
subsystems.role: the treatment selected for the patient's genetic profile.

subsystems.name: Clinical integration
subsystems.role: delivers the result to the doctor and patient and tracks the outcome.

buildSteps.title: Define the clinical question
buildSteps.detail: Decide which disease and which decision the genomic test must inform, such as choosing a drug or avoiding a severe side effect.

buildSteps.title: Collect the sample
buildSteps.detail: Take a blood sample or tumour biopsy with informed consent, then extract DNA in a certified laboratory.

buildSteps.title: Sequence the DNA
buildSteps.detail: Prepare a sequencing library and run it through a high-throughput sequencer, targeting a panel of genes, the exome, or the whole genome.

buildSteps.title: Analyse the data
buildSteps.detail: Align the millions of short reads to a reference human genome, call variants, and filter out common or low-quality changes.

buildSteps.title: Interpret the variants
buildSteps.detail: Classify each variant as pathogenic, likely pathogenic, uncertain, or benign, and match known ones to evidence about drug response.

buildSteps.title: Validate with a diagnostic test
buildSteps.detail: Confirm the actionable mutation using a targeted assay such as PCR or immunohistochemistry that is approved for clinical use.

buildSteps.title: Select and administer therapy
buildSteps.detail: Choose a targeted drug or other treatment, dose it for the patient, and monitor response and toxicity.

buildSteps.title: Track outcomes and update knowledge
buildSteps.detail: Record the result and response in research databases so that future interpretations become more accurate.

prerequisites.why: reading a person's genome quickly and affordably is the foundation of any genetic test.

prerequisites.tech: Reference human genome and variant databases
prerequisites.why: without a reference and population data, a variant cannot be interpreted.

prerequisites.tech: Electronic health records with genomic data
prerequisites.why: linking genotype to clinical outcome at scale requires interoperable records that most health systems still lack.
many mutations have no matching drug, so only some patients can benefit today.
tests and drugs must be approved and paid for before they reach routine care.

pathway.milestone: single-gene tests guiding cancer treatment, such as checking for EGFR or BRCA mutations
pathway.unlocks: better outcomes and fewer side effects for patients with specific tumour types.

pathway.milestone: multi-gene panels and pharmacogenomic testing used routinely before prescribing common drugs
pathway.unlocks: fewer adverse drug reactions and faster selection of effective medicines.

pathway.milestone: polygenic risk scores integrated into screening programmes for common diseases
pathway.unlocks: earlier prevention and more targeted monitoring for those at high risk.

pathway.milestone: real-time genomic monitoring and gene-editing therapies
pathway.unlocks: adaptive treatment that can be adjusted as a disease evolves, with potential for cures in some conditions.
